shared_qualifications: Q1 — Pitting measurements use deaerated synthetic seawater at 90 °C, pH 7.2±0.2 (PDF pp. 1-4). Scan, scratch and current-time methods are distinct (p. 3). The later 21-°C ferric-chloride or 121-°C crevice exposures in Figs. 7-10/21-22 do not redefine the pitting-test electrolyte or temperature. No chloride molarity or reference-electrode offset was inferred; the source values are mV versus SCE.

C1 — The source scan rate 10 mV/min divided by 60 s/min equals 0.1666667 mV/s, compatible with CRA 0.167 after rounding. Table 3 directly reports wt% chemistry; no atomic-fraction conversion is needed. The B-series final treatment is already reported as 1049 °C (1920 °F) on PDF p. 4; the Celsius value is used directly.

Q2 — Table 3 (PDF p. 2) connects F460-F475 compositions to Table 5 A/B specimens. The text on p. 4 assigns B-series a final 1 h at 1049 °C followed by water quenching, consistent with CRA's specific B treatment. A-series matching uses chemistry, method, target group and CRA's generic prior-preparation paragraph; the latter mixes 50-g/50-lb process descriptions, so the exact A-series final treatment is not independently verified. F464 Table 3 Fe/Mn entries also differ slightly from the CSV and are not used as decisive identity evidence.

Q3 — CRA 430 contains no Avg and the exact scan endpoints Min=125.0, Max=142.0 mV. These correspond to F464B runs 1123 (obs_070) and 1134 (obs_067), respectively. Both are supported range members; no mean or midpoint is manufactured. CRA 446's 98-mV scratch value supports both F464B runs 1134 (obs_068) and 1123 (obs_071) under the same condition; the CSV cannot identify which run was used or establish an average. Preserve the separate registered runs and count each shared CRA row once.

Q4 — Obs_085/CRA 451 retains Table 5 F469B scratch=165 mV and Fig. 7 label=265 mV (PDF pp. 3, 5). Its identity is supported by chemistry/method/treatment, but potential agreement is discrepant across presentations. The primary reading is unchanged. Other linked Table 5 primaries exactly equal CRA values; their approximate Fig. 2 readings are compatible at graphical precision. E-Brite's separately registered 128/≈135-mV Table 5/Fig. 2 difference is retained in the unchanged registry; no CRA counterpart is assigned.

Q5 — Composite obs_147 and obs_162-169 retain candidate-only CRA alternatives based on the scratch method, medium/temperature, approximate potential and partial Cr+Mo coordinate. The total is not a full alloy composition; some graph/CRA totals differ, as shown explicitly in paired evidence. These identities remain unresolved without unique specimen/treatment/run labels. All other composite markers were also assessed. Fig. 22's adjacent numbers are weight-loss annotations, not specimen or pitting-potential identifiers. Candidates do not prove repeat experiments or enter default joins.

Q6 — Table 4 plant-test specimens and their heat treatments, Table 2 ternaries/commercial comparisons, current-time bounds, interpolated unmodified bases and additional composite outcomes were all assessed. Unmatched means no defensible counterpart in this supplied CSV, not absence from the paper or extraction failure. All 54 CRA rows have supported Table 5 links. Matching does not identify the source presentation used by original curators and does not certify the database's remaining scientific fields.
